chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Is'haq ibn Ammar who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who buys from the office bearer, and he is an unjust one. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He can buy from him for as long as he does not know that he has been unjust to anyone in it'.

key_terms.الْعَامِلِ: the office bearer / agent / tax collector

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy from an unjust official if I don't know he stole the goods?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'presumption of innocence' in commercial transactions, ruling that buying from an unjust official is valid provided the buyer lacks specific knowledge of the injustice regarding that particular item. It reflects the Shia juristic distinction between general corruption and specific illicit gain, ensuring market stability while holding individuals accountable for their direct actions.
